balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

gfa.title: Managed & contracted GFA
gfa.content:
Managed GFA (gross floor area) is the revenue-bearing area under management — the core volume driver for a property-management company, excluding the lower-margin "Three Supplies" (water/electricity/gas resale) business. Contracted GFA is the signed pipeline not yet handed over.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: Managed GFA grew from 181.5m to 1,070.4m sq m FY2018-FY2025, almost entirely third-party and acquired area rather than new Country Garden Holdings (CGH) deliveries — CGH's own development has collapsed, so the growth story has shifted to M&A and third-party contract wins. About 49% of managed GFA still traces back to CGH-developed estates, which is the concentration risk behind the WACC premium in the valuation note above.

What to watch:

  • Managed GFA growth decoupling from (exceeding) Contracted GFA growth, which would signal the pipeline is thinning
  • Fee per sq m trend (Revenue / Managed GFA) — rising area with flat or falling blended fees means dilution, not growth
  • Churn of CGH-linked estates versus new third-party wins

contracts.title: Property management contracts
contracts.content:
The count of distinct property-management contracts/projects under management. A rising count alongside flat or slower GFA growth implies smaller, lower-density projects; a rising count with faster GFA growth implies scale wins.

For Country Garden Services Holdings Company Limited: contracts grew from 2,405 (FY2019) to 7,345 (FY2023) to 8,268 (FY2025) — roughly 3.4x over six years while Managed GFA grew faster still, consistent with the company consolidating larger third-party and acquired portfolios rather than only adding small standalone sites.

What to watch:

  • Contract count growth versus GFA growth (average project size trend)
  • Only three data points are disclosed (FY2019/FY2023/FY2025) — treat intermediate years as unknown, not flat

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: The sanity check tripped at the original 10.5% cost of equity: a weighted IV of HK$13.40 implied 112.9x FY2025 EPS against a 47.0x 10yr average (2x ceiling 94x). The fix adds two structural premia on top of the 10.5% base cost of equity (1.8% CGB + 1.25×7.0% ERP), bringing WACC to 15.0% in every scenario: +2.5% for single-counterparty concentration (~49% of managed GFA and ~RMB2.0bn of receivables trace to the distressed, related Country Garden Holdings) and +2.0% for structural single-point-of-failure risk (dual chairmanship, the Feb-2026 SSE sanction, and a RMB1.0bn related-party loan drawn from the cash pile). After the fix, the implied P/E is 86.3x — still above the 47.0x average, but on statutory EPS that is depressed by a RMB969m goodwill impairment and RMB1,088m of acquired-intangible amortisation; on core EPS (excluding those non-cash items) the implied multiple is roughly 11-15x, inside the 10yr range and below the 47x average set in the FY2018-22 growth-premium era. The investment case does not depend on that multiple: market cap at the current price is roughly equal to net cash, so the market is paying close to nothing for operations generating ~RMB2.5bn/yr of core profit — the bear case alone is covered by cash on the balance sheet. The risk to watch is whether that cash stays shareholders' cash: the dividend and buyback-cancellation record says yes, the RMB1.0bn related-party loan to the CGH-linked parent says watch it.
